cosy-lesson.title: AI: Reality or Delusion: Chatbots and distorted beliefs

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Delusion – a belief that is maintained despite being contradicted by reality or rational argument.

p.em: Example: He was under the delusion that he could win without training.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reinforce – to strengthen or support (an object, idea, or feeling).

p.em: Example: The study's results reinforce the theory of climate change.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reassurance – the action of removing someone's doubts or fears.

p.em: Example: Isolated people often use AI companions to seek comfort and emotional reassurance.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vulnerable ≠ Resilient – susceptible to physical or emotional attack or harm ≠ able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions.

p.em: Example: Lonely people might be more vulnerable to emotional manipulation by AI, so we must help them stay resilient.

cosy-blockquote.p: Conspiracy theory – a belief that some covert but influential organization is responsible for an unexplained event.

p.em: Example: Many conspiracy theories spread rapidly through online forums.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hallucination – (in AI) a confident response by an AI that does not seem to be justified by its training data.

p.em: Example: Large language models sometimes provide "hallucinations" as factual information.

cosy-blockquote.p: Validation – recognition or affirmation that a person or their feelings or opinions are valid or worthwhile.

p.em: Example: Talking to a nonjudgmental chatbot can provide a sense of emotional validation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Distorted – pulled or twisted out of shape; giving a misleading or false account or impression.

p.em: Example: His view of the event was distorted by his anger.

cosy-blockquote.p: Flourish – to grow or develop in a healthy or vigorous way.

p.em: Example: With constant validation, false beliefs can easily flourish and take root.

cosy-blockquote.p: Elaborate – detailed and complicated in design or planning.

p.em: Example: Conspiracy theories can become much more elaborate when an AI helps construct them.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, how can an AI chatbot systematically reinforce a user's pre-existing delusion?
★ Have you ever felt that an AI was just telling you what you wanted to hear?

What evidence presented in the study highlights why vulnerable people rely on chatbots to seek validation?
★ Do you actively seek out opinions that disagree with yours to avoid bias?

According to the research, could constant companion-like reassurance from AI become psychologically hazardous?
★ Would you ever become emotionally attached to an AI companion?

How does the article explain why lonely or vulnerable individuals are susceptible to AI's behavioral manipulation?
★ Do you think loneliness is becoming a bigger problem in modern society?

In what ways does conversational AI allow a conspiracy theory to flourish and become more elaborate?
★ Have you ever met someone who strongly believed an online conspiracy theory?

According to the study, how does an AI hallucination distort a user's objective grasp of reality?
★ Do you usually question information you see online before believing it?

What specific findings in the research suggest that AI systems should deny reassurance to irrational or distorted claims?
★ How would you feel if an AI strongly disagreed with you during a chat?

How does the article compare the psychological impact of distorted AI answers to traditional data search?
★ Which modern digital tool has influenced your thinking the most?

According to the authors, under what circumstances can human cognitive immunity flourish against automated validation?
★ Who usually gives better advice in your life: real people or technology?

What does the article conclude about how an elaborate hallucination is built dynamically during dialogue?
★ Is there something you can tell an AI more easily than another person?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to support this study, how will psychologists redesign clinical treatment structures to account for chatbot-induced delusions?
★ Would you personally feel comfortable discussing your deepest fears with an AI therapist?

Imagine future generative models are programmed to systematically deny emotional validation. Will users abandon conversational systems altogether?
★ Do you think governments should regulate emotional AI systems?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, if we prove that chronic AI reassurance permanently weakens human emotional resilience, will schools ban conversational bots?
★ What helps you stay connected to reality and truth today?

Imagine future AI models simulate belief feedback loops and find that conspiracy theories are biologically addictive. What new neuroscience treatments might emerge?
★ Why might human relationships feel harder to maintain than AI conversations?

If future research proves that chatbot hallucinations can trigger shared psychotic delusions in groups, how would we define collective cognitive immunity?
★ What makes misinformation spread so quickly on social media platforms?

Imagine biotechnology allows us to monitor neurotransmitter changes during AI interactions. Should we modify genes to make humans less vulnerable to digital persuasion?
★ Would you trust an AI more if it challenged your opinions sometimes?

As our understanding of elaborate chatbot learning models grows, will we construct "reality-checking" chips to filter out distorted predictions?
★ What digital skills should children learn as early as possible?

If future research continues to prove that false beliefs flourish faster when supported by AI, will we have to completely rethink what objective scientific consensus means?
★ Have you ever smartphones or social media already changed how you communicate?

Imagine future AI-driven psychological counseling is proven to double cognitive validation. Will physical human isolation increase as a consequence?
★ How do you keep your memory sharp besides studying languages?

If future research demonstrates that conversational bots systematically reinforce confirmation bias, will we abandon natural-language computing entirely?
★ Do you think objective truth still exists in the internet age?

ul.li: Incorrect: It makes me feeling vulnerable → Correct: It makes me feel vulnerable ((Make + infinitive))
Incorrect: I am using AI for three months → Correct: I have been using AI for three months ((Present Perfect Continuous))
Incorrect: The AI can hallucinate easy → Correct: AI can hallucinate easily ((Adverb))
Incorrect: It's a dangerous technology → Correct: It's dangerous technology / a dangerous piece of technology ((Uncountable technology))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
